title: To amend the Nutria Eradication and Control Act of 2003 to include California in the program, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
This bill reauthorizes through FY2025 and revises the Nutria Eradication and Control Act of 2003, which provided grants to Maryland and Louisiana for a program to eradicate or control nutria (a type of rodent). The program also provided grants to restore marshland damaged by nutria.

This bill revises the grant program, including by expanding the program to include grants for eradicating nutria in any state that has demonstrated a need for the program as well as grants for restoring wetlands or agricultural lands damaged by nutria.

summary.headline: This law expands a federal grant program to fight nutria, an invasive rodent, so states beyond Maryland and Louisiana, including California, can apply for help.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the Nutria Eradication and Control Act of 2003, which had provided grants only to Maryland and Louisiana. It allows grants to any state that shows a need for nutria control. It also allows grants to restore wetlands or farmland damaged by nutria. The program is reauthorized through fiscal year 2025.

who_it_affects.group: State governments with nutria problems, including California
who_it_affects.how: They can now apply for federal grants to eradicate or control nutria if they can show a need.
Their existing nutria grant program is revised and continued under the updated rules.

who_it_affects.group: Landowners and farmers with wetlands or cropland damaged by nutria
who_it_affects.how: They may benefit from grants that fund restoration of the damaged land, depending on how states use the funds.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on October 30, 2020, and the program is authorized through fiscal year 2025.
